reproduceNotice: Regenerates the historical evidence inventory and this presentation extract offline. Never fetches live catalog content, changes snapshots or notices, or generates runtime kit YAML. Does not update HTML.
extractMaintenance: Review all site HTML measurement tables, activation cases, totals, citations, and dated references against the regenerated JSON. Review historical source pins, licenses, hashes, arithmetic, and methodology before sharing. These fixtures do not describe the current remote catalog inventory.

methodology.bytes: Exact UTF-8 bytes, Buffer.byteLength; no tokenizer used.
methodology.lines: LF-separated logical lines; no phantom empty line after a final LF; empty text is zero lines.
methodology.body: Every character after closing frontmatter delimiter LF, including the following blank line.
methodology.discovery: name + LF + parsed YAML description + LF; not an observed host prompt. Ponytail description retains its trailing LF.
methodology.exclusions: Full skill counts exclude license, SOURCE notice, optional Codex policy metadata, host wrappers, paths, system prompts, tools, history and retained activations. Disk totals are not prompt totals.
methodology.limitations: Assumed activation cases for historical fixtures only; not runtime token counts, benchmarks, universal savings, identical host loading policies, or current remote catalog measurements. These selected snapshot directories contain no required external supporting Markdown/scripts/binaries. Complete supporting-file hashes are in the evidence inventory.

sources.name: Matt Pocock: to-questionnaire
sources.description: Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in.

sources.name: Anthropic: frontend-design
sources.description: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.

sources.name: DietrichGebert: ponytail
sources.description: Lazy senior dev mode: the smallest change that fully solves the task, and a reply a busy human understands in one read. Use on any coding task (writing, fixing, refactoring, reviewing, choosing dependencies) and when the user says "ponytail", "be lazy", "simplest solution", "yagni", or complains about over-engineering or bloat. Levels: lite, full (default), ultra.

instructionsComparison.limitation: Different real upstream instructions, not byte-equivalent to the skill. Their size difference is not equivalent-content savings.
